tagline: Through the old No Man's Land, once a haven for outlaws.
intro: This is mostly flat country, first settled by the Atakapa and Coushatta. After the Louisiana Purchase nobody could agree where the western border ran, and France, New Spain, Mexico and the United States all had a claim on it. People called it No Man's Land, and land pirates and outlaws found it a comfortable place to be.

The drive starts at Burr Ferry, where LA 8 meets LA 111, and heads south. Keep on down LA 111 and it comes to Merryville, four miles from the Sabine River and Texas. From there US 190 runs north and east about 19 miles to DeRidder.

moments.title: Burr Ferry
moments.text: After Natchez fell and Alexandria burned, trenches and breastworks went up here against an attack that never came, and their remains can still be seen.

moments.title: Merryville
moments.text: The town keeps the grave of Charles Smith, called Leather Britches, who fought in its union strike and died in an ambush, a hero or an outlaw depending on who in Merryville tells it.

moments.title: Beauregard Parish Jail
moments.text: DeRidder's Gothic Revival jail, with a spiral staircase up to the cells and a tunnel to the courthouse, took on the name Hanging Jail after 1928 and is open now for tours.
